content: Reliance Retail recorded its highest-ever quarterly footfalls of over 282 million across 18,700 stores. Grocery and consumer electronics saw strong festive uptake. Jio digital services delivered 11.2% YoY revenue growth with average revenue per user (ARPU) expanding to Rs 181.7. Management reiterated capex moderation over the next 4 quarters as 5G network rollout reaches completion, freeing up operating cash flows.

In the Oil-to-Chemicals (O2C) segment, gross refining margins (GRM) normalized to $10.5/bbl due to higher crude premiums and Red Sea shipping rerouting costs. Downstream petrochemical demand remained subdued due to slower Chinese economic reopening. Downside risks are mitigated by feedstock flexibility and integration across gasification assets.

Tata Consultancy Services confirmed signing of a $1.2 billion contract with UK's Nest scheme over an initial 10-year term. The engagement leverages TCS BaNCS platform to transform pension administration operations. Deal total contract value (TCV) in the quarter stood at $8.1 billion, with North American client discretionary spending showing stabilizing trends.

EBIT margin expanded by 50 basis points to 25.0% despite seasonal furloughs, supported by improved realization, pyramid optimization, and dropping LTM attrition to 13.3%. Management expects generative AI pipeline to double by H2 FY25 with over 100,000 employees certified in modern AI tooling.

HDFC Bank disclosed its roadmap to normalize the Credit-to-Deposit (CD) ratio down from 110% towards 85-88% over 3 to 4 years. Management will prioritize retail deposit mobilization over accelerated wholesale loan growth. Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) stood comfortably at 110%, with average CASA deposits registering 37.7% of total deposits.

Gross non-performing assets (GNPA) stood at 1.26%, reflecting resilient retail underwriting. Contingency buffers and floating provisions aggregate to over Rs 15,000 crore. Unsecured personal loans and credit cards represent under 10% of total advances, with average credit scores exceeding 760 across new originations.

Infosys revised its FY24 constant currency revenue guidance downward to 1.5% - 2.0% (previously 1.0% - 2.5%) citing unexpected client reprioritization, budget deferrals, and project cancellations in communications and financial services verticals. Operating margin guidance was maintained at 20% - 22% via Project Maxima cost optimization.

CEO highlighted large deal signings of $3.2 billion with 71% net new scope. However, transition velocity from booking to revenue recognition has lengthened by 60 to 90 days as enterprise customers insist on phased milestone rollouts. European banking exposure remains the most conservative geography.

[STALE CONTRADICTORY REPORT] Infosys management projects sustained double-digit discretionary revenue acceleration of 14% to 16% over the multi-year digital transformation super-cycle. Client spending in high-margin consulting is expected to outpace core maintenance without signs of budget curtailment.

ITC Limited received no-objection approvals from stock exchanges for the demerger of its Hotels Business into ITC Hotels Limited. Under the scheme, ITC shareholders will directly hold 60% in the new hospitality entity with ITC retaining a 40% stake, unlocking shareholder value and boosting ITC's return on capital employed (ROCE).

Cigarette segment net revenue grew 3.6% YoY with underlying volume stability following rational Union Budget taxation. FMCG-Others revenue expanded 7.6% driven by Aashirvaad, Sunfeast, and Bingo, with EBITDA margin scaling 100 bps YoY to 11.0%. Rural distribution reach expanded to 2.4 million direct outlets.

State Bank of India reported standalone net profit of Rs 9,164 crore after absorbing one-time pension liabilities of Rs 7,100 crore. Gross NPA declined 72 bps YoY to 2.42%, the lowest in over a decade. Return on Assets (ROA) annualized reached 0.94% (excluding wage revision impact, ROA surpassed 1.05%).

SBI's Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) stood robust at 13.05% with Tier-1 capital at 10.58%. Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR) including written-off accounts improved to 91.54%. Management reiterated credit cost guidance below 50 bps for FY24, expressing confidence in corporate loan demand across renewables, roads, and battery chemicals.

ICICI Bank recorded core operating profit growth of 11.7% YoY. Return on Equity (ROE) annualized held at an industry-leading 18.5%, with Net Interest Margin (NIM) at 4.43%. Domestic loans grew 18.8% YoY led by retail and SME financing, while maintaining spotless credit discipline across unsecured loans.

Over 92% of personal loans and 86% of credit cards are now disbursed digitally via pre-approved data analytics models. Non-ICICI Bank account holders using the iMobile Pay app crossed 10 million. Cost-to-income ratio improved to 40.6% supported by AI-assisted back-office reconciliation.

Larsen & Toubro consolidated order book crossed an all-time record of Rs 469,800 crore, up 22% YoY, with international orders comprising 39%. Major wins in Middle East renewable solar plants and domestic high-speed rail corridors provide 3-year revenue visibility. Working capital to revenue ratio improved to 16.6%.

[STALE CONTRADICTORY REPORT] L&T cautions that international execution across the GCC is severely stalled due to localized component shortages, labor repatriation, and raw material inflation, warning of imminent project write-downs and protracted multi-year delays across civil infrastructure jobs.

Tata Motors solidified its domestic EV market leadership with over 73% market share. Launch of the Acti.ev dedicated EV architecture in the Punch.ev delivered 421 km certified range. Management approved corporate restructuring to demerge commercial vehicles and passenger vehicles into two independent listed entities to unlock operational focus.

Jaguar Land Rover delivered record Q3 EBIT margin of 8.8%, generating free cash flow of GBP 623 million. Net automotive debt reduced sharply from Rs 57,000 crore to Rs 29,000 crore, on track to achieve net zero automotive debt by FY25. Defender and Range Rover order bank stood at 148,000 units.

[CRITICAL RISK DISCLOSURE] Despite strong market demand and breakout vehicle deliveries, Tata Motors and JLR remain vulnerable to single-source specialty semiconductor microcontrollers and Red Sea maritime shipping disruptions. Prolonged transit times add GBP 45 million in freight expense per quarter, while potential EU anti-subsidy tariff adjustments pose margin headwinds for UK export platforms.

Sun Pharma's global specialty revenue expanded 21.4% YoY to $240 million, now accounting for 19.2% of consolidated sales. Ilumya (plaque psoriasis), Cequa (dry eye), and Winlevi (acne) continue gaining dermatological prescription share in the US and Europe. R&D spend was sustained at 6.2% of revenues.

US FDA completed a Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) inspection of the Halol formulation facility issuing 3 procedural observations under Form 483. The company is submitting a comprehensive corrective action plan within 15 business days. Halol facility supplies approximately 2.5% of total US sales, limiting immediate top-line financial impact.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) recorded net purchases of Rs 24,500 crore in Indian equities in Q1 2024. Capital Goods, Automobile, and State-run Banks received 68% of fresh allocations, while Information Technology and FMCG faced sector rotation outflows due to global rate uncertainty and rich domestic multiples.

India's real GDP growth for Q3 FY24 printed at a surprising 8.4%, anchored by manufacturing gross value added (GVA) of 11.6% and central government infrastructure capital expenditure. Private corporate capex shows broad-based revival across metals, cement, automotive, and renewable energy sectors.

The RBI Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously to keep the policy repo rate unchanged at 6.50% while maintaining the stance of withdrawal of accommodation. Food price shocks continue to require vigilance, though core inflation moderated to 3.5%, providing support for sustained financial sector stability.
